author: blu
body: The HttpClient builds HTTP request messages and parses status lines, headers and response bodies. It does not send anything: it has no effect row, it cites nothing that touches the wire, and every function here is a pure transformation of bytes. It used to say it sent them over a TCP connection via the NetworkStack, which was never true. Net chapter HttpFetch is the chapter that sends.

author: blu
body: The requests it builds are HTTP/1.0, not 1.1 -- http-serialize-request writes the version -- and the close-delimited body that 1.0 implies is what HttpFetch's receive loop is built around.

author: blu
body: The length the server declared, read out of the header bytes, or -1 when it declared none. This is what lets a reader stop at the end of the body instead of waiting for the connection to close, and it is the only thing that can tell a complete body from a truncated one. http-parse-response cannot: its content-length field is the length of what arrived, so it agrees with itself whether or not the whole body did.
